title: Hamlet's Mill on ancient knowledge of precession

tellings.quote: very ancient very early knowledge of of precession.

plain: Hamlet's Mill, a book written in the 1960s by Giorgio de Santillana and Hertha von Dechend, argues that ancient myths carry "very ancient, very early knowledge of precession," the slow wobble of the Earth that shifts the stars' positions over thousands of years. The writer Graham Hancock tells Michels about the book in his own summary, without quoting it. If its case holds, early peoples tracked the sky far more precisely than usually believed.
